Sanofi sent Medivation an unsolicited, non-binding $52.50 per-share proposal in April 2016. The board rejected it on 04/29 and Sanofi then launched a consent solicitation to replace the board, while Pfizer expressed interest from May. In late June Medivation's bankers began a sale process under confidentiality and standstill agreements with several parties, including Sanofi, which withdrew its consent solicitation. Pfizer bid $65.00 in cash in the preliminary round on 08/08 and was invited on 08/10, with several other parties, to a definitive round with a draft merger agreement. Pfizer raised its bid to $77.00 on 08/19 and gave a best-and-final $81.50 on 08/20; the agreement was signed that afternoon and announced 08/22. Rival bids are not reported in this bidder-side filing.

cells.Question: Sanofi's Type: should it be Strategic rather than Unknown?
cells.Why, with page: The filing names Sanofi and its CEO and reports its proposal, consent solicitation and confidentiality agreement (pp. 21–22) but never describes its business. The instruction bars outside knowledge, and Sanofi is not a formal bidder or the winner.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Strategic on all Sanofi rows; round 0 and round 1 would then have only strategic named bidders.

cells.Question: Is Sanofi's consent solicitation to replace the board an Activist event rather than Other material event?
cells.Recommended answer: Keep Other material event; Initiation stays bidder-led.
cells.Why, with page: Sanofi acts as a hostile bidder pressing its own $52.50 proposal (p. 22); the filing does not establish that it is a shareholder, which the Activist label presumes.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Row 9 becomes Activist and Deal facts Initiation could read 'activist-influenced' or 'mixed'.

cells.Question: Process and round map: one process; round 0 (04/15–06/27), round 1 opened 06/28, round 2 opened 08/10 and ran to signing, including the best-and-final request. Is that right?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. Most plausible alternative: a round 3 opened 08/19 by the 'best and final' request, moving rows 26–31 into round 3.
cells.Why, with page: The 08/14 letter already sought a Merger Agreement mark-up and a definitive proposal (p. 23), a binding-stage request, so the 08/19 request (p. 24) reads as an improvement request within it. Gaps of two months or more without acquirer contact: none (longest 05/20–06/28/2016). E5: (a) fails, (b) fails, (c) n/a — no second process.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Round 3 would hold Pfizer's $81.50 alone; round 2 would become Not final with a single due date 08/19. Opening round 1 on 06/29 (invitation) instead moves only row 10's date.
